pages.text:
HTSI Interview Experience
Pranjal Rathi
Third Year
Information Technology
Location: Pune
Stipend: 80,000 INR.
Timeline
Online Test
The test had 61 questions for 90 mins in total and was held on Mettl, we had to allow camera
and microphone access.

Coding Section
The United Nations Organization released an official document regarding the most
important events from the beginning of time (dated 00-00-0000) with a brief description
of the events. The date of all the events is mentioned in the DD-MM YYYY format
Find the total number of distinct years referenced in the document.
Input Specification:
input1: String containing the content of the document
Output Specification:
Return the total number of distinct years referenced in the document.
Example 1:
input1: UN was established on 24-10-1945. India got freedom on 15-08-1947.
Output: 2
Explanation:
2 distinct years, 1945 and 1947 have been referenced.
Solution: I gave a brute force solution for this question, which seemed the best to me at
that moment. We need to iterate over the string till i<length -9 and check if the
characters are present in the sequence of numbers(n) such that nn-nn-nnnn, then
extract the years part and insert it in an unordered_set. In the end, return the size of the
unordered_set.
Aptitude Section
This section had a 30-minute timer. The questions were quite easy; you just needed to
think quickly and solve them fast, as there were 30 questions to complete in 30 minutes.
Some were mental ability questions, english grammar related, while others required

math (probability and statistics). The math questions were a bit challenging, so it's
better to solve the non-math questions first.
Computer Fundamentals
This section had questions based on -
DSA
-6
OS
-6
OOPs -7
CN
-6
DBMS -5
I finished my online assessment with around 10-15 minutes remaining and just to make
sure I hadn't missed any question, I double-checked for anything remaining and also
double-checked the answers and then submitted the assessment.
Around 27 students were shortlisted for interviews. We received the shortlist around
4:30 PM on the next day (1st August), and the interviews were scheduled for 9 AM on
2nd August. That day I reached home from college around 5 and had not checked any
messages till then. My friends congratulated me and after that I checked the mail. After
around 15 mins, I started preparing for the interview.
Interview Preparation
I started by reading previous year interview questions. This step is very important. One
should without fail be going through the past year interview experiences. From there, I
learned that they ask more about OOPs concepts and DBMS and I had seen no OS
related questions. So I started with OOPs, followed by DBMS, DSA questions and kept
the OS for the last. I got the idea of answering HR questions from the past year interview
experience itself. The preparation time just flies by, you don't get to know when the clock
struck 12. I had done OOPs, DBMS by then. I didn’t really revise my DSA notes. I had

gone through some of it 2-3 days back. Then I slept around 12:30 am so that I have
sufficient rest for the big day. We reached college by 8:30am. In between the
preparation, our TPO crs had asked us to give the resume we uploaded. In case if you
want to make any changes to that, then make them and send that. We were asked to
take both the uploaded and the updated one. I gave the updated resume to the
interviewer.
Note: Always verify your resume and seek preparation guidance from your seniors.
INTERVIEWS (Offline)
Technical Round
We were seated in the TPO hall and introduced to the panelists who came to interview
us, consisting of seven people, one of whom was from HR. The technical rounds ran
simultaneously, with one interviewer assigned to each candidate. We were called in
batches of three, and those deemed capable were sent directly for the HR round after 15
minutes to an hour of technical interviews (so be prepared for the HR round as well). I
was 16th or 17th in the serial order, and my turn came just after the lunch break, around
1:45 PM. Don't forget to ask those who go for the interview before you about the
questions they were asked, as sometimes the questions get repeated.
Finally, I was called in and greeted warmly by the interviewer. Always greet the
interviewer with a smile and be confident. She took my resume and asked me to
introduce myself. Be prepared with your introduction and try to rehearse(don’t mug it up
just keep in mind the flow of the intro) 1-2 times before going for the interview. My
introduction was not more than a minute. Try to keep the duration about 45-60 secs.
The flow should be:
1. Name
2. Branch

3. CGPA (not necessary but if u have a good cgpa, then consider mentioning).
4. Technical stacks/domains you've worked on (I focused on web development)
5. Achievements (hackathon wins, competitive programming awards)
6. Positions in clubs/internship experience
7. Hobbies
My interviewer seemed impressed by my introduction. She asked me for my resume and
then proceeded to ask me about how I had solved the OA coding problem solution. (This
was not mentioned in the previous year interview experience so be prepared for any new
questions that come.). She also asked me about how my OA went, which I told her was
pretty good. Just the math questions including graphs were a bit tough and there was a
little less time towards the end of the aptitude round as it had a timer. This must have
given the assurance that I solved the questions on my own(as I mentioned the
difficulty).
After this, she asked me achievement and project related questions. Know everything
about the things you put in your project and resume as they ask in detail. After that she
asked me a DSA question - doubly linked list - to delete the target node from the list. She
asked me to write that code on paper. Interviewers want you to think out loud and so did
I. I was writing the code, where in between i asked her if i can take an example for my
reference which would make it easier to write the code. She was friendly and allowed
me; she also told me to complete the code and then show it to her. So here I wasn't
thinking out loud and completed the code and explained to her. Then she asked me
questions on OOPs. First question was to explain runtime polymorphism with examples
and pseudo code(Reference - C++ Polymorphism - GeeksforGeeks). Second was about
friend function in c++ (Refernce - Friend Class and Function in C++ - GeeksforGeeks).
Then she asked me which data structure was I comfortable with and suddenly I couldn’t
remember the names of the data structures, but she was really nice to then name a few
like - heaps, to which i answered no as i had not done that data structure (always be
honest with your answers, and don’t hesitate to mention things you haven't done—they
won't focus on those areas), trees- to which i answered yes and she asked me about

difference between trees and binary trees. Then she asked me if I could explain to
her how the quicksort algorithm works. After that she asked me to write the code for
it. She seemed satisfied with all the answers I gave her.
She then proceeded to ask the river crossing puzzle of cabbage, goat and wolf.(
Reference - Farmer Crosses River Puzzle - Solution (mathsisfun.com))
After this she asked me if I had any questions. I asked her about what her best day at
HILTI was like. In between, I also mentioned how I liked HILTI - as it is a product based
company and told them I had gone through their website and that I liked the products.
This showed that I was actually interested in joining and working there as an intern.
After this, we were done with the interview round. I thanked her for taking my interview.
My interview went for around 45-50 mins, but the time inside there flew by, you don’t get
to know how much time went there.
Note:
> Be calm and confident. Keep a smile on your face.
> Know your OA coding solution. Don’t give any other answer as they open your solution
and cross verify.
> Be clear about the objectives of your projects, what you did to achieve them, and the
technical details involved.
> Know what you’ve put on your resume. You should know all about it.
> Don’t fumble by thinking of various ways to solve the problem. Start with brute force
calmly, the interviewer will smoothly guide you through.
> It's important to always scroll through the company's website and gather information.
> Be sure to prepare your questions based on this research (always ask questions—it
shows that you're genuinely interested in the company).
> Make sure to ask relevant questions and try to come up with something unique, rather
than just the common questions you find on the internet.
> Practice famous puzzle problems - like bucket filling (2 others were asked about it)
,etc.

HR Round
My HR round started in about 5 minutes after my technical interview ended. The HR
interviewer asked me if my name was Pranjal, to which I replied yes. She then asked me
to introduce myself and asked about my family background. She seemed impressed by
my introduction and said that’s pretty much a lot of things. Hearing this, I was really
happy and it boosted my confidence. After that, she asked me my I chose science
(related to family background answer).
She asked about my biggest failure, is chatgpt considered boon or bane and also asked
about the difficulties faced while working on a project. Next, about the location - Pune, if
I had ever visited Pune? Would I be able to live in Pune and how do I find it? Asked me
about the soft skills mentioned in the resume. After that, if I'm gonna do masters or
plans for higher studies to which i answered no. She asked if I had any questions for her.
I asked her the same question as I asked in the interview round. Here also in the
conversation, I mentioned about me going through the official website of HILTI and how
I found the work culture and products at Hilti. She seemed impressed by that. After this,
the HR round was over. I thanked her for taking my interview.
I then went outside to the TPO hall and waited calmly with my friends for the results.
Around 5:30 PM, the HR along with her team came to announce the results. When she
called my name, I was overwhelmed with joy and was surprised as we couldn’t predict
who they would select. Everyone's interview had gone almost the same. The feeling of
being selected was one of pure jubilation.
4 other candidates were offered internships along with me.
Note:
> If your elder sibling is studying for masters, don’t mention that; as they assume you
would also be going for masters. This reduces your chances to get selected.
Resources

1. For DSA, I used Striver's a2z sheet, some people also consider another
popular option, DSA450. I made notes for each topic because DSA is a long
journey and it's easy to forget what was covered earlier. Also maintain the habit
of giving CP contests.
2. For OS and DBMS, I studied thoroughly during the 4th semester and made notes
at that time. These notes, created using the Gate Smashers playlist for both
subjects, proved to be quite helpful later. The day before the interview, I reviewed
InterviewBit PDFs, which were in a question-and-answer format and are also
quite useful. (PDFs for React, mongoDb, SQL, OOPS are also available on
interviewBit). For SQL, there's also a website named MariaDB tutorial that is
well-organized and explains SQL in an easy manner.
3. For OOPs, I started with the one-shot video of OOPs in C++ from Apna College
but found it necessary to study further using GeeksforGeeks (GFG) articles.
Remember to study pointers and other C++ concepts if you're working with C++.
Also, be prepared for questions like the difference between C++, Java, and C.
4. For HR preparation, many suggest Indiabix. While it’s a useful resource, I
recommend figuring out your own answers to commonly asked HR questions.
Having a unique perspective and avoiding generic answers can make a big
difference.
Pranjal Rathi
Hilti Intern
